objective: Run the uncommitted codex/calitree-implementation worktree's evidence-based referral (calitree_v3_evidence prompt + fixed-rule evidence_policy) live on the same 120-case dev slice as this worktree's v2 baseline, for a direct accuracy/referral comparison.
prompt_diff: Byte-identical across all 5 prompt files (initial_rubric.txt, extract_components.txt, merge_prompts.txt, gradient_feedback.txt, conflict_resolver.txt) except one appended block in initial_rubric.txt asking the model to also self-report conditions_visible/evidence_contradictory/edit_incomplete_vs_undeterminable in the same JSON response. Verified by direct diff.

global_selection_guard.note: Both runs independently rejected TextGrad's global warm-start rewrite in favor of the plain seed prompt, because the rewrite scored worse on held-out balanced validation accuracy.

actual_root_fallback_rate_n352.bug_found: Codex's _routing_inference_metrics computes root_ids from a `tree` argument that is None at eval time (calitree_eval has no prompt_tree input socket), so root_ids is always an empty set and the fallback_to_root_rate check never fires, silently reporting 0.0 regardless of the true rate. Same root cause makes tree_metrics.overall.structure always null. Verified by directly counting routed_node == 'global:initial' in the train report's predictions dict: 164/352 = 46.59%.

leaf_merge_optimization_divergence.note: TextGrad leaf specialization and merge synthesis DID rewrite prompt text substantially in both runs (verified: all 22/22 leaves in my run have prompt text different from the seed template). This is real optimizer output, not identical to the seed. However, since both runs' global_selection guard rejected the rewritten warm-start prompt, the majority-case classifier (the global root, ~47-55% of cases) reverted to the literal unmodified seed text in both systems, so roughly half the accuracy difference above is attributable to the one prompt-text difference (plus noise), and the other half (routed-to-leaf/merged-branch cases) reflects independent, stochastic TextGrad rewrites rather than a controlled comparison.

bugs_found_in_codex_worktree: tree_metrics.overall.structure is always null in a live calitree_eval run because the eval node never receives prompt_tree (same as fallback_to_root_rate bug above).
fallback_to_root_rate always reports 0.0 for the same reason, contradicting the true rate (46.6% verified by direct count).
conclusion: Not a clean architecture A/B: the tree-building algorithm (CaliTreeBuilder) is identical code in both worktrees, run in the same replace mode. The measured differences trace to (a) one appended prompt paragraph affecting ~half the cases via the seed fallback, and (b) independent stochastic TextGrad optimizer output for the other half. Codex's richer self-reported referral signal fires marginally more than my structural signal (2 vs 0 of 352) but neither is a working referral policy at this scale. This is a third independent data point (with the delta-tree and two-gate results) that TextGrad's global rewrite does not survive its own validation guard.
